title: Seeded warmup and KV shadowing playbook for multi-region model onboard
content:
Context:
This is a working playbook for onboarding large new autoregressive models (vX) into production with minimal KV cache shock to regional fleets. Goal is to define a seeded warmup + shadowing strategy that reduces cold-KV misses during rollout while keeping GPU headroom predictable. Informal, expect numbers to be refined after a sampling run.

Summary of approach:
1) Traffic sampling -> derive top-20k prefixes to seed (per region)
2) Seed KV cache on a small warmup pool (warmup pods per region) for a configurable window prior to traffic cutover
3) Shadow traffic to warmup pool (no responses served) to fill model KV footprint for heavy prefixes
4) Ramp main fleet gradually while maintaining warmup pool until KV hit-rate stabilizes
5) Fallback: route to compatible quantized variant if cache miss spike or latency SLO breach

Key assumptions (update after sample run):
- Model vX average token length: 90 tokens (inference tail heavy)
- Typical per-request prefix unique tokens to hold in KV: 2.3k tokens
- Avg token size in KV (packed): 1 byte/token post-quantized KV encoding (approx) -> rough KB conversions below.
- Target warmup hit-rate threshold before full cutover: 85% for seeded prefixes, 60% overall

Sample calculations (example region: us-west-2)
- Measured baseline peak RPS for similar model (vW): 120 RPS sustained (serving 3-model mix)
- Expected peak RPS post-rollout with vX (40% traffic shift): 48 RPS additional

KV footprint per active user prefix (conservative):
- Prefix tokens to keep: 2300 tokens -> ~2.3 KB (packed) -> round to 3 KB/active prefix to include metadata
- Seed top prefixes targeted: 20,000 -> 20k * 3 KB = 60,000 KB = ~58.6 MB per region seeded
- Add overhead (index, eviction buffer): x1.6 -> ~94 MB total seeded KV memory per region

GPU warmup capacity (us-west-2 example):
- Warmup pool config (recommended start): 4 x p4d-like instances (32 GPU-equivalent vnodes) serving only warmup/shadow traffic.
- Expected KV warming throughput of pool: ~300 prefixes/sec (measured in lab for vX on p4d-equivalent)
- Time to seed 20k prefixes: 20,000 / 300 ≈ 67 seconds (plus padding for eviction/replication) -> plan 5 minutes window
- GPU-hour cost for warmup window: 32 GPUs * (5/60) hrs ≈ 2.67 GPU-hours per region warmup event

Regional scaling notes (table form, approximate):
- us-west-2: extra RPS 48 -> seed 20k prefixes -> warmup pool 4 instances -> 2.7 GPU-hrs
- eu-central-1: extra RPS 28 -> seed 12k prefixes -> warmup pool 3 instances -> 2.0 GPU-hrs
- ap-southeast-1: extra RPS 16 -> seed 8k prefixes -> warmup pool 2 instances -> 1.3 GPU-hrs
(These numbers are conservative; adjust after real sample-run latencies and KV throughput measurements.)

Operational playbook (step-by-step)
- T-72h: Run distributed traffic sampler (sample 7 days of real traffic) -> produce per-region prefix frequency list and TTL distribution (artifact: samples/prefixes-<region>.csv)
- T-48h: Compute seed set (top N per region) using weight thresholding (script: infra-ops/tools/seed-picker.py). Review with SE/solutions team for customer-specific prefixes (HIPAA/PCI customers may need explicit exclude list).
- T-24h: Provision warmup pool (autoscale group locked to desired instance count). Add warmup policy tags and route config in rollout plan (Console route flag: warmup=true).
- T-4h: Start shadowing traffic (no responses) to warmup pool at 10% sampled rate to verify KV write paths and replication latency. Monitor KV write QPS, eviction, and memory.
- T-1h: Increase shadowing to 50%, validate hit-rate climbing for seed prefixes and tail stability. Watch for GC/ejection metrics.
- Cutover: Start 10% traffic to vX main fleet + continue warmup. Ramp main fleet traffic 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 30-minute intervals if latency and error budgets allow.
- Post-cutover T+1h: Keep warmup pool for additional 2 hours of grace; if seeded hit-rate >= 85% and total KV miss delta < 15% of baseline, deprovision warmup nodes gradually.

Monitoring and signals to abort/rollback:
- Token latency P95 increases > 1.5x from baseline sustained for 5 minutes -> pause ramp, increase warmup shadowing to 100% (if capacity)
- KV miss-rate increase > 2x baseline for > 10 minutes -> rollback to previous model and escalate to infra on-call
- GPU saturation (utilization > 92%) -> stop further ramp, add reserved burst capacity or route to quantized fallback

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Eviction storms: Throttle warmup write QPS, increase seed TTLs for important prefixes, or reduce seed set size.
- Regional replication lag: Prefer local-only seeding; avoid cross-region prefill unless using global KV replication with measured lag < 200ms.
- Unexpected traffic patterns (tail index blowups): Have an emergency quick-roll policy to pin traffic to previous model and spin up a larger warmup pool to absorb prefixes.

Cost/back-of-envelope for a 3-region rollout (seed 40k total prefixes across three regions):
- Total GPU-hrs (warmup): ~6 GPU-hrs (across regions) -> rough cloud cost = 6 * $3.25/hr (example) ≈ $19.5 per rollout event (very rough, unit cost varies by instance type/commit)
- Additional KV memory seeded: ~260 MB total (negligible relative to fleet sizes)

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Validate actual per-prefix KV size for vX with the new packing format (ask applied-ml to run encode_size job: AM-encode-2026)
- [ ] Run end-to-end warmup test on staging with real traffic replay (owner: Rina)
- [ ] Add a per-customer exclusion list for seeded prefixes (privacy/compliance check with Security)
- [ ] Extend playbook to support cascading multi-model onboard (two models back-to-back)

Quick reference commands and artifacts:
- seed-picker script: infra-ops/tools/seed-picker.py --region us-west-2 --top 20000 -> outputs csv
- warmup ASG blueprint: infra/provision/warmup-asg.yaml (branch: infra-warmup-blueprint)
- Debug dashboard: Console -> Observability -> Fleet -> Warmup Pool (look for kv_seeded_count, kv_hit_rate_by_prefix_bucket)
- Slack channel for rollout chatter: #infra-model-rollouts (ping on-call: @miguel)

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep seed set small enough to avoid eviction cascade but large enough to cover 80% of warmup writes (tradeoff).
- Consider two-phase seed: heavy hitters (top 2k) seeded 24h prior, long tail 20k seeded in T-4h window.
- For dedicated customers with predictable traffic, consider customer-specific pin and pre-seed only that tenant's prefixes to save memory.

End of doc - working draft. Update after the staging warmup run on 2026-02-24.
